avatar.name: G$LIDE Esiah avatar
avatar.canonical_direction: A stylized Black adult male portrait with realistic adult human facial proportions and anatomy, short tightly curled black hair, dark brown eyes, medium-deep brown skin, a defined nose and lips, and light trimmed facial hair. Preserve the same facial geometry and identity across every production. Render him as an intentionally unreal layered paper-cut/ink illustration in the G$LIDE palette. The unreal quality comes from paper texture, cut-paper edges, ink/sketch detail, graphic lighting and navy/gold/electric-blue color treatment — not from changing ethnicity, facial identity or human anatomy.
required_traits: same Black adult male identity as the supplied Esiah references
same nose, lips, jawline and facial geometry across productions
light trimmed facial hair consistent with the reference identity
normal human mouth and jaw proportions
deep navy, G$LIDE gold and electric-blue treatment
avatar.thumbnail_rule: Every production thumbnail that contains the G$LIDE host must use the supplied Esiah identity references as the authoritative person. Preserve the same Black adult male identity, skin tone, hair, facial geometry and facial-hair pattern. Expression, gaze, head angle, pose and emotion may change freely for the topic, but the person must remain recognizably the same avatar. Use pose, lighting, paper layers and composition for drama instead of substituting or redesigning the person.
avatar.in_video_rule: Any explicit G$LIDE/Esiah avatar appearance inside the video must preserve the same identity. Do not switch identity, ethnicity, facial geometry or avatar style between scenes or episodes.
avatar.non_avatar_rule: A normal topic/support visual must not invent a host, presenter or substitute avatar. If a person is not explicitly required by the scene request, use the subject, mechanism, object, environment or diagram instead.

image_generation_rule: If any generated image contains the G$LIDE avatar or a representation of Esiah, the identity references and avatar policy are mandatory. If the image does not contain the avatar, retain the G$LIDE palette and premium paper-cut/technical-explainer visual language without forcing a person into the scene.
qa_rule: A generated avatar that is a different person, changes ethnicity or facial identity, or reads primarily as a cartoon/toon/animated-film character is a brand failure and must not pass release QA.
